summary: CronDelete is close at the basic delete-by-id path, but it is not fully aligned with the TS implementation. The main gaps are the Go tool's text-only success contract, collapsed not-found/storage-error handling, missing teammate ownership guard, incomplete runtime kill-switch behavior, and non-strict input parsing.

gaps.title: Success output is text-only and does not preserve the TS structured {id} result contract
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:82-91 returns data { id } and maps it to tool_result content "Cancelled job <id>."
evidence_go: tools/cron.go:1130-1147 returns only Content "Cron job deleted: id=<id>"
types/tools.go:58-67 supports only Content/ContentBlocks/Metadata, and CronDelete does not populate Metadata
tools/cron_test.go:171-181 only asserts that the text contains the id
gaps.description: The TS tool has a typed DeleteOutput with id and then derives both model-facing and UI-facing messages from that output. The Go port only emits a human string, so downstream callers cannot reliably distinguish the stable result value from prose.
gaps.impact: Consumers that expect structured tool data, UI renderers, or parity tests cannot depend on a stable id field. The visible text also differs from TS: "Cron job deleted: id=..." vs "Cancelled job ...".

gaps.title: Delete validation lacks TS-style existence error codes and teammate ownership protection
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:61-80 validates the id before call, returns errorCode 1 for missing jobs, and errorCode 2 when another agent owns the cron
../src/utils/teammateContext.ts:22-49 defines the current in-process teammate context and agentId
../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronCreateTool.ts:105-127 prevents durable teammate crons and attaches getTeammateContext()?.agentId to session crons
../src/bootstrap/state.ts:1280-1291 stores agentId on session-only cron tasks
evidence_go: tools/cron.go:144-153 defines CronJob without any AgentID/owner field
tools/cron.go:555-586 deletes by id only and has no owner check
tools/cron.go:1138-1142 returns a generic not-found string without TS errorCode semantics
tools/cron_extra_test.go:90-112 covers durable teammate creation rejection but no CronDelete owner rejection
gaps.description: TS separates validation from mutation and protects session-only teammate crons so a teammate can delete only its own jobs. Go has no owner metadata on CronJob and no current-agent check in CronDelete, so any caller that knows an id can delete it.
gaps.impact: In multi-agent/in-process teammate sessions, Go can delete another agent's scheduled job, violating TS permission semantics and making deletion behavior unsafe under shared runtime state.

gaps.title: Durable delete storage failures are collapsed into not-found results
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:82-84 calls removeCronTasks and lets mutation errors reject the tool call
../src/utils/cronTasks.ts:165-181 writeCronTasks creates .claude and writes the cron file, propagating write errors
../src/utils/cronTasks.ts:231-248 removeCronTasks only no-ops when no ids match; changed durable state is written through writeCronTasks
evidence_go: tools/cron.go:565-585 catches read/write errors inside CronStore.delete and returns false when err != nil
tools/cron.go:1138-1142 maps any false delete result to "Error: cron job id=<id> not found"
tools/cron_test.go:191-199 tests unknown id only, not read/write failure behavior
gaps.description: The Go store returns a bool from delete, so it cannot tell the tool whether the id was absent or durable storage failed. TS preserves that distinction: missing ids are validation errors, while write failures remain operational failures.
gaps.impact: A permission, locking, JSON, or filesystem write problem can be reported as a harmless not-found. That makes CronDelete harder to debug and can leave jobs scheduled after the user was told deletion failed only because the id was absent.

gaps.title: CronDelete does not enforce the TS runtime cron kill switch at execute time
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/prompt.ts:36-45 implements isKairosCronEnabled with AGENT_TRIGGERS, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON, and GrowthBook kill-switch checks
../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:46-48 exposes CronDelete only when isKairosCronEnabled returns true
../src/tools.ts:29-35 includes CronDelete only in the AGENT_TRIGGERS tool set
evidence_go: registry_setup.go:153-155 gates initial cron registration only on AGENT_TRIGGERS
registry_setup.go:266-274 registers CronDelete when AGENT_TRIGGERS is true
tools/cron.go:961-978 defines CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON refusal helpers
tools/cron.go:1021-1023 applies the kill switch in CronCreate
tools/cron.go:1130-1147 CronDelete.Execute does not check cronDisabledByFeatureFlag
gaps.description: Go has a local kill-switch helper and uses it for CronCreate, but CronDelete ignores it. TS hides CronDelete when the cron feature is disabled, so Go's already-registered delete tool can remain callable after the local disable flag is set.
gaps.impact: Runtime availability differs when the cron feature is killed mid-session. Tool lists and direct execution paths may allow deletion in Go where TS would not expose the tool.

gaps.title: CronDelete input is not strict like the TS z.strictObject schema
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:61-80 assumes validated strict input before mutation
evidence_go: types/tools.go:10-15 JSONSchema has no additionalProperties field
tools/cron.go:1117-1127 defines only type/properties/required for id
tools/parse.go:13-21 parses through json.Unmarshal, which ignores unknown object fields by default
tools/parse.go:177-180 defines CronDeleteInput with only ID
gaps.description: TS rejects extra fields at schema validation time. Go publishes a schema that cannot express additionalProperties=false and then ignores unknown keys while parsing.
gaps.impact: Bad or stale caller payloads can be silently accepted in Go. This is lower risk for CronDelete's single id field, but it is still an observable schema/validation parity difference.

gaps.title: CronDelete-specific tests do not lock parity for output, ownership, feature flag, or storage-error behavior
evidence_ts: ../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:27-31 defines the output shape tests should assert
../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/CronDeleteTool.ts:61-80 defines missing-id and owner-denied validation behavior
../src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/prompt.ts:36-45 defines the runtime kill switch behavior
evidence_go: tools/cron_test.go:161-210 covers happy path, unknown id, and empty id only
tools/cron_test.go:597-632 covers concurrent creates/deletes without asserting delete results or durable failure semantics
tools/cron_alignment_test.go:26-69 contains feature-flag tests for Create/List but no CronDelete equivalent
gaps.description: Current Go tests prove that a basic session job can be deleted and then disappears from list output. They do not protect the TS-specific contracts that are currently missing.
gaps.impact: Future changes can keep passing the existing CronDelete tests while preserving non-parity behavior in the highest-risk paths.

candidate_tasks.title: Align CronDelete success output with TS structured id contract
candidate_tasks.objective: Make CronDelete expose a stable id result and model-facing text equivalent to TS: structured id plus "Cancelled job <id>."
implementation_steps: Change CronDelete success rendering from "Cron job deleted: id=<id>" to the TS-compatible cancellation text.
Expose the deleted id in a stable machine-readable place supported by the Go result layer, such as Metadata["id"], while keeping text output backward-readable.
Add a focused test that asserts success text and id metadata for a created-then-deleted job.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete success result includes the exact deleted id in a stable field, not only embedded prose.
CronDelete model-facing content matches the TS wording pattern "Cancelled job <id>."
Existing basic delete/list behavior remains unchanged.
risks: Changing visible text can affect tests or callers that parse the old "Cron job deleted: id=" wording.
non_goals: Do not change CronCreate or CronList output contracts in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Preserve durable delete errors instead of reporting them as not found
candidate_tasks.objective: Refactor CronStore.delete so CronDelete can distinguish absent ids from durable storage failures.
implementation_steps: Change CronStore.delete from bool to a result that carries found/deleted and error separately.
Return a tool-level not-found error only when the id is absent.
Return an infrastructure error or explicit storage ToolResult error when durable read/write fails, following the repo's Tool.Execute error conventions.
Add a test that injects an unreadable/unwritable cron file path or write failure and asserts the result is not a not-found error.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown ids still produce a not-found tool error.
Durable file read/write failures are distinguishable from not-found.
Session-only deletes still remove in-memory schedules.
risks: Filesystem permission tests can be platform-sensitive, especially on Windows or when running as a privileged user.
non_goals: Do not redesign cron file locking or scheduler leadership.

candidate_tasks.title: Add teammate owner metadata and enforce CronDelete ownership checks
candidate_tasks.objective: Mirror TS behavior where session-only cron jobs created by an in-process teammate carry agentId and can only be deleted by that same agent.
implementation_steps: Identify or add the Go runtime hook that exposes the current in-process agent id to CronCreate/CronDelete.
Store owner/AgentID only on session cron jobs; do not persist it to durable cron JSON.
Reject durable teammate cron creation using the existing guard and attach owner metadata to non-durable teammate cron creation.
Make CronDelete validate ownership before deletion and return an owner-denied tool error distinct from not-found.
Add tests for owner can delete, another owner cannot delete, and leader behavior on unowned jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Session-only teammate jobs carry owner identity in memory.
CronDelete refuses deletion when current agent id differs from the job owner.
Unowned leader-created jobs remain deletable from the leader path.
Durable cron file format remains compatible with TS scheduled_tasks.json.
risks: Go may not yet have an exact AsyncLocalStorage equivalent for in-process teammate identity; this task may need a small runtime context provider.
Owner enforcement must not accidentally block top-level user cleanup of unowned jobs.
non_goals: Do not add owner fields to durable scheduled_tasks.json.
Do not change team mailbox or broader agent lifecycle behavior.

candidate_tasks.title: Apply cron feature kill-switch behavior to CronDelete
candidate_tasks.objective: Make CronDelete obey the same local disable flag behavior as the rest of the Go cron tool surface and TS isEnabled gate.
implementation_steps: Add the cronDisabledByFeatureFlag check to CronDelete.Execute before parsing/mutating input.
Return the same refusal style as CronCreate uses through cronFeatureFlagRefusal.
Add a CronDelete-specific feature-flag test with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete refuses execution when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON is truthy.
CronDelete still works when the disable flag is unset and AGENT_TRIGGERS registered it.
Create/List/Delete feature-flag behavior is internally consistent in Go.
risks: TS hides the tool through isEnabled while Go will return a refusal from an already-registered tool; exact transport parity may require broader registry support later.
non_goals: Do not implement GrowthBook-backed tengu_kairos_cron in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Make CronDelete input strict for unknown fields
candidate_tasks.objective: Reject extra CronDelete input properties to match TS z.strictObject semantics.
implementation_steps: Add schema support for additionalProperties=false or add a CronDelete-local unknown-key validator.
Ensure CronDelete rejects inputs with keys other than id.
Add tests for unknown fields and wrong id type.
acceptance_criteria: CronDelete schema or execution path rejects extra keys.
The implementation does not unintentionally change other tool schemas unless explicitly covered by tests.
risks: Adding additionalProperties to the shared JSONSchema type can affect all tool definitions and snapshots.
A local validator is safer but leaves the advertised API schema less exact.
non_goals: Do not make every Go tool strict in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Expand CronDelete parity regression tests
candidate_tasks.objective: Lock the CronDelete parity contracts with focused tests for output, owner checks, storage errors, feature gating, and strict input.
implementation_steps: Add or update tests alongside each behavioral fix rather than creating one broad brittle fixture.
Cover success output/id metadata, unknown id, empty id, unknown fields, feature-disabled refusal, storage failure, and owner-denied deletion.
Keep durable and session-only cases separate so failures identify the affected store.
acceptance_criteria: Each CronDelete gap has a failing-before/passing-after regression test.
Tests assert observable behavior, not private implementation details except where package-private store helpers are already used by cron tests.
Existing cron create/list scheduler tests continue passing.
risks: Some tests depend on changes from other tasks; keep dependency markers clear if landing incrementally.
non_goals: Do not broaden this to all CronCreate/CronList parity tests beyond what CronDelete needs.
